title: CCSDPD bust alleged drug house near 4 Las Vegas valley schools - NewsBreak
text:
By Joshua Peguero ,
4 hours ago
LAS VEGAS (KLAS) — Several law enforcement agencies busted an alleged drug house, located near four Clark County schools, where police say children visited to buy drugs.
Clark County School police surveilled the house located near Valley View Boulevard and Washington Avenue for about a year. It began with a tip from administrators and parents at Robert O. Gibson Leadership Academy. Officers soon noticed dozens of people, including middle schoolers, buying drugs.
>>Download the 8 News Now Vegas streaming app Investigators captured photos of reported drug deals happening at the house, and in some cases, children were caught leaving. The house is located within walking distance of Helen M. Smith Elementary, McWilliams Elementary, Gibson Middle School, and Western High School.
CCSDPD arrested Jeremiah Cochran and charged him with contributing to delinquency/negligence of minor; sell/supply/prescribe controlled substances in presence of children; two counts of owner/possessing gun by prohibited person; and possession to sell scheduled I/II substances.
Police said evidence included Instagram photos Cochran uploaded holding guns, money, and marijuana.
According to a police report, Gibson Principal Christopher Gist told officers there was a suspicious house that he had “observed adults arrive at the residence and never go to the front door. Instead, they approach the garage side of the door and conduct ‘business’ there.”
Gist said, “He has seen an uptick in marijuana vape pens at Gibson Middle School and he believes it is due to the residence,” according to the arrest report.
Investigators placed a teen in custody after leaving the house on March 3. According to an arrest report, the teen identified himself as a Western High School student, and police found marijuana on him. Several days later, on March 10, SWAT executed a search warrant on the house and arrested Cochran.
Cochran reportedly told officers that around 30 to 50 people a day contact him to buy narcotics. He said most of his young customers were family referrals and he “will do transactions with mothers, fathers, and children,” the report said.
When pressed by police on selling drugs to children, Cochran said he will only sell to them “during the hours of ‘5 p.m. to 9 p.m,’,” according to the arrest report. He claimed to have made $30,000 a month in drug sales.
CCSDPD said inside Cochran’s house, they seized a handgun; rifle; 15 pounds of marijuana; 3.4 pounds of THC concentrate; 60 grams of cocaine; 205 grams of mushrooms; and 103 THC vape pens.
Cochran is currently out on bail. Court records show he’s scheduled to appear before a Las Vegas Justice Court Judge in July.
